key_terms.meaning: A pair of terminals where the current entering one terminal equals the current leaving the other, so only one current variable is needed.
A linear network with two such pairs: an input port (port 1) and an output port (port 2).

key_terms.term: Port variables V1, I1, V2, I2
key_terms.meaning: The four external quantities; V1 and I1 at the input port, V2 and I2 at the output port, with I2 usually drawn leaving the network.
The impedance seen looking into one port, for example Zin = V1/I1 with the other port terminated.
V1 = z11 I1 + z12 I2 and V2 = z21 I1 + z22 I2; z11 = V1/I1 with port 2 open.
I1 = y11 V1 + y12 V2 and I2 = y21 V1 + y22 V2; y11 = I1/V1 with port 2 shorted.
V1 = h11 I1 + h12 V2 and I2 = h21 I1 + h22 V2; h21 is the short-circuit current gain.
I1 = g11 V1 + g12 I2 and V2 = g21 V1 + g22 I2; the inverse of the h set.
V1 = A V2 - B I2 and I1 = C V2 - D I2; written with the output current reversed, so cascades multiply.
The set that expresses V2 and I2 in terms of V1 and I1; its matrix is the inverse of the ABCD matrix.
Rewriting the same two linear equations to make a different pair the unknowns, giving one set from another by algebra.
Port 2 of one two-port feeds port 1 of the next; the overall ABCD matrix is the product of the individual matrices.
Ports joined so voltages add (series, Z matrices add) or currents add (parallel, Y matrices add).
A network of R, L, C and transformers only, with z12 = z21, y12 = y21, h12 = -h21, and AD - BC = 1.
The two ports are interchangeable, so z11 = z22, y11 = y22, h11 h22 - h12 h21 = 1, and A = D.
A rational function that is real for real s and has Re[F(s)] ≥ 0 for Re(s) > 0; the test for a realisable driving-point function.
A partial-fraction expansion of Z(s) or Y(s) into series or parallel L, C and parallel-resonant branches; first Foster and second Foster forms.
Continued-fraction expansion of Z(s) or Y(s), giving a ladder of series arms and shunt arms; first and second Cauer forms.

takeaways: A two-port is a black box described by only two equations linking four external variables, so any two of the four can be chosen as inputs.
All six parameter sets are the same two linear equations rearranged; pick the set whose measurements are easiest in the lab or whose interconnection rule is simplest.
Z parameters are measured with a port open, Y parameters with a port shorted, h parameters with a port shorted and open mixed, ABCD with the output open and shorted.
Series adds Z matrices, parallel adds Y matrices, cascade multiplies ABCD matrices, and each rule holds only if the interconnection does not disturb the port currents or voltages.
Reciprocity is a property of networks without dependent sources; it shows up as equal off-diagonal terms in Z and Y and as AD - BC = 1 in ABCD.
Symmetry is about the network looking the same from both ends; it gives z11 = z22, y11 = y22 and A = D but says nothing about the transfer terms.
Network synthesis is the reverse of analysis: it asks whether a given Z(s) or Y(s) can be built, and the answer is yes only if the function is positive real.
Foster and Cauer forms turn a positive real reactance function into a circuit of L and C by partial fractions or by continued fractions, and both give the same input impedance.
bank_note: Long answers usually ask for full derivations of the parameter sets plus the conditions under which the series, parallel and cascade rules are valid, so write the defining equations, the measurement conditions and the interconnection conditions together.

bank.q: Define a two-port network and explain why only four external variables are needed. Define each of the four port variables and state the sign convention used for I2.
outline: Port: two terminals with equal and opposite currents
Two ports means four terminals and four variables V1, I1, V2, I2
I2 drawn leaving port 2 so the network obeys the passive sign convention
Linearity means the relations between the variables are linear
Uses: filters, transformers, transmission lines, transistor small-signal models

bank.q: Define the Z parameters of a two-port. Give the defining equations, state how each parameter is measured, and explain why they are called open-circuit parameters.
outline: z11 = V1/I1 with I2 = 0 (port 2 open)
z12 = V1/I2 with I1 = 0
z21 and z22 similarly
Units are ohms; reciprocal condition z12 = z21; symmetric condition z11 = z22

bank.q: Define the hybrid parameters and explain why they suit transistor modelling. Write the equations and give the meaning and unit of h11, h12, h21, h22.
outline: h11 input impedance with output shorted, in ohms
h12 reverse voltage gain with input open, dimensionless
h21 forward current gain with output shorted, dimensionless
h22 output admittance with input open, in siemens
Mixed variables match transistor input current and output voltage

bank.q: Define the ABCD parameters, state their measurement conditions, and explain why the output current is reversed in the definition.
outline: V1 = A V2 - B I2, I1 = C V2 - D I2
A = V1/V2 with port 2 open, dimensionless
B = V1/(-I2) with port 2 shorted, in ohms
C = I1/V2 with port 2 open, in siemens
D = I1/(-I2) with port 2 shorted, dimensionless
Reversed current makes the output port current of one block equal the input port current of the next, so cascades multiply

bank.q: State the reciprocity and symmetry conditions for Z, Y, h and ABCD parameters and explain what each property means physically.
outline: Reciprocal: z12 = z21, y12 = y21, h12 = -h21, AD - BC = 1
Reciprocity holds for networks of R, L, C and ideal transformers without dependent sources
Symmetric: z11 = z22, y11 = y22, h11 h22 - h12 h21 = 1, A = D
Symmetry means swapping the ports leaves the network behaviour unchanged
Symmetry does not imply reciprocity and reciprocity does not imply symmetry

bank.q: A T network has series arms Za and Zb and a shunt arm Zc. Derive its Z parameters, then find its ABCD parameters.
outline: Write mesh equations for the two loops
z11 = Za + Zc, z22 = Zb + Zc, z12 = z21 = Zc
Convert with A = z11/z21, B = delta z / z21, C = 1/z21, D = z22/z21
delta z = z11 z22 - z12 z21
Check reciprocity AD - BC = 1

bank.q: Two two-ports with ABCD matrices M1 and M2 are cascaded. Prove that the overall matrix is M1 M2, and use this to find the ABCD parameters of two identical sections in cascade.
outline: Write equations for each block with reversed output current convention
Output voltage and current of block 1 equal input of block 2
Matrix product follows by substitution
For identical sections square the matrix
State the condition: the interconnection must not alter the port currents

bank.q: The Z parameters of a two-port are given. Derive the expressions for input impedance and output impedance when the output is terminated in ZL and the input source has impedance ZS.
outline: Termination gives V2 = -I2 ZL
Similarly Zout = z22 - z12 z21/(z11 + ZS)
Limits: ZL infinite gives z11; ZL zero gives the short-circuit input impedance

bank.q: Convert a given set of h parameters into Z parameters and then into ABCD parameters, showing every algebraic step.
outline: Start from V1 = h11 I1 + h12 V2 and I2 = h21 I1 + h22 V2
Solve the second equation for V2 in terms of I1 and I2
Substitute into the first to get z11, z12, z21, z22
Use A = z11/z21, B = delta z/z21, C = 1/z21, D = z22/z21
State the determinant relations used, for example delta h = h11 h22 - h12 h21

bank.q: A driving-point impedance Z(s) = (s² + 4)/(s² + 1) is proposed as an LC impedance. Test whether it is positive real and realise it in Foster form if it passes.
outline: Check that coefficients are real and positive
Check poles and zeros on the imaginary axis, simple and alternating
Check residues at poles are real and positive
Partial fractions give a series of parallel LC branches (first Foster)
Comment that a valid LC function has poles and zeros that alternate on the jω axis

bank.q: Compare the Z, Y, h and ABCD parameter sets for measurement convenience, ease of cascading and use in transistor circuits, and state which set you would choose in each of three practical situations.
outline: Z: open-circuit measurement, good for series connection
Y: short-circuit measurement, good for parallel connection, natural for admittance calculations
h: mixed short and open measurements, standard for transistors, used in feedback analysis
ABCD: output open and short measurements, multiplication for cascade
Choose ABCD for transmission lines and filter chains, h for transistor amplifiers, Y for parallel admittance banks

bank.q: Explain the conditions under which the series, parallel and cascade interconnection rules are valid, and describe what happens to the parameters when the conditions fail.
outline: Series: the same current must flow through both ports at each side, checked by the port test
Parallel: the same voltage must appear across both ports at each side
Cascade: the current leaving one block must equal the current entering the next
If port conditions fail, the composite network is not described by the simple sum or product
Mention the use of a transformer or hybrid coil to enforce the conditions

bank.q: State the necessary and sufficient conditions for a rational function to be a positive real driving-point impedance function, and use them to judge whether a given function can be synthesised as an RC network.
outline: F(s) real for real s
No poles in the right half plane; jω-axis poles simple with real positive residues
Re[F(s)] ≥ 0 for Re(s) > 0
For RC functions, poles and zeros are simple, negative, real and alternate, with the nearest critical frequency to the origin a pole of Z
Conclude with a clear yes or no and the reason

bank.q: A lossless LC one-port is to be built with a given reactance function. Obtain both Foster forms and one Cauer form, and compare the number of elements and the sensitivity to component spread.
outline: Foster first form: partial fractions of Z(s), series of parallel LC branches
Foster second form: partial fractions of Y(s), parallel of series LC branches
Cauer first form: continued fraction of Z(s), ladder network
Cauer second form: continued fraction of Y(s), dual ladder
Both forms realise the same impedance; ladder has fewer elements, Foster forms have less mutual dependence between element values

glossary.def: A linear network with two pairs of terminals, described by two linear equations in the four port variables.
A pair of terminals carrying equal and opposite currents.
A Z parameter measured with one port left open so that its current is zero.
A Y parameter measured with one port shorted so that its voltage is zero.
The ratio V/I at the same port, with the other port terminated in a stated way.
The ratio of a voltage at one port to a current at the other, as in z21 and z12.
A parameter of a set that mixes voltage and current on each side, such as h11 (ohms) and h21 (dimensionless).
An element of the ABCD matrix that relates input voltage and current to output voltage and current.
A parameter of the set giving output variables in terms of input variables, the inverse of the ABCD matrix.
The property that the transfer parameter from port 1 to 2 equals the transfer parameter from 2 to 1.
The property that the two ports of a two-port can be interchanged without changing its behaviour.
A connection in which the output port of one two-port becomes the input port of the next.
A connection in which the corresponding port voltages of two networks add while the port currents stay equal.
A connection in which the corresponding port currents add while the port voltages stay equal.
The design of a network of R, L and C elements that realises a prescribed driving-point or transfer function.
A rational function that is real for real s and has non-negative real part in the right half plane.
A polynomial whose roots all lie in the left half of the s plane.
A realisation obtained by partial-fraction expansion of a reactance or susceptance function.
A ladder realisation obtained by continued-fraction expansion of an impedance or admittance function.
A chain of series arms and shunt arms, the natural result of Cauer expansion.
The property of LC and RC functions that poles and zeros interleave along the negative real axis or the imaginary axis.
